questions.q: What's the key difference between troubleshooting and tuning, per this lesson?
options: Troubleshooting is reactive (fixing an active incident); tuning is proactive and deliberate (making a system measurably faster whether or not it's currently broken)
They are exactly the same activity with different names
Tuning only applies to Azure SQL Database, not on-prem SQL Server
Troubleshooting is always more valuable than tuning
questions.explain: Troubleshooting responds to a live incident; tuning is a deliberate, ongoing discipline independent of whether anything is currently broken.

questions.q: What are the four steps of the systematic tuning loop this course is built around?
options: Measure, identify, change, verify
Guess, change, hope, move on
Alert, escalate, restore, document
Backup, restore, patch, reboot
questions.explain: Every technique in the course plugs into this loop: establish a baseline, find the specific bottleneck, make one change, then measure again to confirm it worked.

questions.q: Why is adding an index that speeds up one report query but isn't measured against write performance NOT a good example of tuning, per this lesson?
options: A change made without measuring first can make things worse overall — like silently slowing down every write to that table — while still feeling like it helped
Adding indexes is never a valid tuning technique
Report queries should never be optimized
Write performance is irrelevant to tuning work
questions.explain: Without measuring the full before/after picture, a change can quietly cost you somewhere else even as the targeted symptom improves.

questions.q: What is a 'baseline,' as this lesson defines it?
options: A recorded 'normal' state of key metrics, used to judge whether a change actually helped
The single slowest query on a server
A synonym for a full database backup
The default SQL Server installation configuration
questions.explain: A baseline is what lets you know, objectively, whether a later measurement represents an improvement — without one, 'faster' is just a feeling.

questions.q: What is the single most common mistake this course exists to correct, per this lesson?
options: Skipping straight to making a change without measuring first
Measuring too many metrics before making any change
Using execution plans at all
Documenting findings after a fix
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly calls out jumping straight to a fix — without a measured baseline or a targeted bottleneck — as the mistake the whole course's methodology corrects.
